referenceName: Dentologie: airy neighborhood studio with warm color and service photography

source.name: Dentologie official website

source.rightsEvidence: Requester-attested clearance for internal full-page desktop/mobile screenshot retention, derived prompts, and pipeline-model visual-reference use. No source-owner written grant was attached; see rights/requester-attestation.md.

conversion: contextual appointment actions after service choices

referenceDna.annotatedDescription: The official multi-location dental-practice site uses a compact quiet header, a centered short editorial promise with appointment and call actions, then a large interior photograph. A brief philosophy chapter pairs a human-scale image with concise copy. Three photographic service choices lead into a manually controlled patient-review moment, a fresh-color reassurance band, an image-led neighborhood-office strip, a second narrative chapter, a compact secondary-services row, patient questions, and a dark contact close. Mobile turns the narrative into a single-column sequence and keeps each booking action close to its decision point. The brand, images, people, reviews, claims, office facts, and exact visual trade dress are source-only.

heroGeometry.alignment: centered text opening followed by a wide image, then asymmetric narrative chapters
heroGeometry.viewport: compact navigation, short promise, service-area context, two actions, and first image form the opening

navigationGeometry.placement: quiet top edge above the centered opening
navigationGeometry.mobile: compact logo and menu control with the booking route kept easy to reach

typography.display: high-contrast editorial serif with occasional italic emphasis
typography.scale: short centered hero, quiet utility labels, comfortable paragraph measure, restrained chapter headings

palette.contrastIntent: quiet text on light fields with saturated chapter surfaces used sparingly for hierarchy

servicePresentation.interaction: each primary choice links to its substantive service explanation and the next relevant action; secondary services remain scannable text links

ctaPlacement.early: both routes appear beside the opening promise, with appointment actions repeated after service decisions

motion.library: native controls and CSS where sufficient; no source scripts transferred

mobileRecomposition.strategy: centered opening followed by single-column editorial chapters
rules: place the hero image directly after the opening controls
stack philosophy image and copy without overlap
make one service item visible per carousel state with labeled controls
wrap insurance or trust marks only when verified and supplied
keep location imagery compact and prevent page-level horizontal overflow

prohibitedPatterns: copying source brand, logo, copy, photographs, people, reviews, ratings, insurance marks, or exact trade dress
inventing office locations, services, insurance participation, prices, hours, credentials, appointment availability, or patient outcomes
a repeated wall of identical rounded cards
a privacy banner covering the hero
hidden content that depends on motion or autoplay
mobile carousels with inaccessible offscreen controls

requiredSignatureElements.description: short centered editorial promise and two useful actions followed by one large practice image
a small set of primary service choices using contextual photography
one saturated surface chapter that resets the page rhythm before later decisions

acceptanceChecks: The opening shows a concise practice promise, a primary action, and a useful secondary route.
A large contextual practice image is separated from the text rather than used as a generic stock background.
Primary services are easy to distinguish and not repeated as a second identical card wall.
FAQs and contact remain distinct, directly navigable sections.
At 390 px, images, service choices, and controls fit with no horizontal page overflow.
No source identity, photo, patient statement, location, or unsupported medical claim is reused.

review.notes: Complete archive alternative retained outside the fixed six-reference dental production pool. Full-page screenshots were inspected after lazy media and offscreen sections were rendered; no broken images, page errors, or width overflow were observed. It is not part of the production core or registry. Requester-attested clearance is not represented as an independently verified source-owner grant.
